book: Chapter I, §2.4 (p. 6, the boundary of the tube T_(I,J), corrected sign): moving the parameter r_j, which stands after s + 2(j - s - 1) parameters of the list theta_1, ..., theta_s, r_(s+1), theta_(s+1), ..., r_n, theta_n, to the front (the outward normal first, §1.3) is the permutation Fin.cycleRange of that place, of sign (-1)^s for every j; the printed sign (-1)^j fails for n = 1, s = 0, j = 1.
limitations: The combinatorial sign of the permutation only: no chain, orientation of a manifold or boundary is formalised; that the boundary piece carries the orientation of the remaining parameters is the convention of §1.3. Stokes' formula for these tubes (f = z, n <= 3) is checked in checks/sage/ch1.py, section S2.

book: Chapter II: the identity behind the lemma of §5.5 (p. 21): for g = A f, det A f = adj(A) g, i.e. f_1 det A = sum_k (adj A)_(1k) g_k, so det A lies in I_P(g) where f_1(P) != 0; the example of §5.6 (p. 25, corrected sum over i <= j): the matrix with twos on the diagonal and ones elsewhere has determinant n + 1 and is nonsingular for all n, the printed all-twos matrix is singular for n >= 2, and (n + 1) n / 2 - 1 > n for n >= 3; the inequalities of the proof of the lemma of §5.3 (p. 18): |w| > eps gives |w - t zeta| > eps - t |zeta|, and |w - t zeta| = eps - t |zeta|, t <= 1, |zeta| < eps give |w - zeta| >= eps - |zeta| > 0; the step of the proof of the lemma on a displaced distinguished boundary (§8.1, p. 39): |f| >= r, |g| <= rho, delta < r - rho give |f + g| > delta.
limitations: Algebraic identities over an arbitrary commutative ring (the germs at a point), determinants over Q, and inequalities for single complex numbers (the values of f_j, g_j, zeta_j at one point); no holomorphic function, ideal of germs, chain, homology or residue is formalised. The residues of the chapter (transformation formula, formula (4) of §5.5, the functionals of §5.6, the global residues of §8) are checked on examples in checks/sage/ch2.py.

book: Tsikh (1992), Chapter III: the limits along admissible paths of §11.1 (p. 65; for two consecutive radii, eps_2 -> 0 and eps_1/eps_2^q -> 0 for all q, eps_1^a eps_2^b tends to 0 for a > 0 and to infinity for a < 0, and is 1 when all exponents vanish: hence 'not all zero'); the sign of formula (1) of §13.3 from Stokes' formula of the proof and the convention dT(psi) = (-1)^(r+1) T(d psi) of §3.3 (pp. 84-85; corrected (-1)^(j+p+1), the printed (-1)^p of the proof refuted); the sets I_k of the proof of the lemma of §13.4 (pp. 86-87: columns chosen in them are distinct, giving a normal alpha_A; if one is empty, a single K gives formula (1) of the proof); the inequality of Lemma 1 of §12.2 (p. 69); the negative exponents b_j of Step 5 of §12.4 and of the lemma of §12.5 (pp. 79-81).
limitations: Bounded steps only: the admissible-path lemma is proved for two consecutive coordinates of the path (the reduction of a product over all coordinates to them is not formalised; checks/sage/ch3.py checks the lexicographic rule for three coordinates and exponents in {-2, ..., 2}); the values of the currents are elements of a commutative ring and Stokes' formula with the boundary (-1)^j T_(I, empty) is a hypothesis taken from the book; the identification of the supports with the planes P_A, the existence of the currents, the measure-theoretic limits of §12 and the resolution of singularities are not formalised (the combinatorics of (8)-(10) are checked exhaustively for small matrices in checks/sage/ch3.py).

book: Chapter IV: the proof of the WPT in §16.4 (p. 114, (7)-(9), with the corrected |z_j| < delta_2): the Hefer matrix of (f(zeta) - f(z), z) with respect to (xi - zeta, eta - z) is block triangular [[P(xi, zeta), -P(eta, z)], [0, 1]], so its determinant is det P(xi, zeta); formula (5) of §18.1 (p. 136, corrected without 1/p!): the complex Hessian of (1/2) log(|z|^2 + eps) has determinant c^n (1 - c t) = eps/(t + eps)^(n+1), c = 1/(t + eps), for every n (matrix determinant lemma); the proof of Bezout's theorem in §19.1 (p. 142): Euler's formula k_j g_j = sum_q z_q dg_j/dz_q gives g = A z with det A = (k_1...k_n)^(-1) dg/dz; the lemma of §20.1 (p. 149, corrected condition p + n != q): given Euler's identities for P and Q, sum_j d_j(z_j P/Q) = (p + n - q) P/Q, the coefficient of d sigma; the end of the proof of the theorem of §20.3 (pp. 155-156): d_n (d_1...d_(n-1)) = d_1...d_n, the exponent of R^*(u) = u^(-d_1...d_n) R(u) once mu_1 + ... + mu_r = d_1...d_(n-1), and |alpha| >= mu - d_1...d_n + d gives |alpha| - d >= mu_(a_k)(f^*) for every zero a_k when the mu_(a_k)(f^*) sum to mu - d_1...d_n (including |alpha| = beta).
limitations: Algebraic identities over a commutative ring or a field and inequalities of natural numbers: the Hefer coefficients, the Hessian entries, the values of the partial derivatives and the multiplicities are given as data, and Euler's identities and the sum of the multiplicities (the lemma of §20.3) are hypotheses; no holomorphic function, current, integral, residue, local algebra or multiplicity is formalised. The total mass 1 of ((i/pi) ddbar log|z|)^n (volume and radial integrals), the residues and multiplicities of the chapter and the examples are checked in checks/sage/ch4.py.

book: Chapter V, §23.2: the lemma (p. 174): on the finite part of the chain c_+ (Im z_1 >= 0, z_2 real) Im(a_j z_1 + b_j z_2 + c_j + i r_j) = a_j Im z_1 + r_j > 0 for a_j >= 0, r_j > 0, and Im phi_(j-) < 0 on c_-; in the chart z'_1 = 1/z_1 with a_j > 0, b_j = 0, a point of F_(j+-) = {a_j + (c_j +- i r_j) z'_1 = 0} has Im z'_1 = +-a_j r_j/(c_j^2 + r_j^2) (the corrected sign; the printed sign fails for a = r = 1, c = 0), while Im z_1^(-1) <= 0 on c_+ and >= 0 on c_-, so F_(j+-) misses c_+-; the proof of the theorem (p. 174): |i - z|^2 - |i + z|^2 = -4 Im z, so the Cayley map w = (i - z)/(i + z) takes {Im z > 0} to {|w| < 1} and R to {|w| = 1}, and the domain {|w_2| > 1} is {Im z_2 < 0}; formula (3) (p. 173, corrected half-planes) on G = 1/(x_1^2 + 1)(x_2^2 + 1): the Jacobian of (f_-, f_+) is -4 at (-i, i) and 4 at (i, -i), and (2 pi i)^2 (-1/4) = pi^2, (2 pi i)^2 (1/4) = -pi^2.
limitations: Statements about complex numbers only: the linear functions, the chart coordinate and the Cayley map are evaluated at given points; no divisor, chain at infinity, cycle, orientation, integral or residue is formalised, and the value pi^2 of the integral is not proved here (pi is an arbitrary complex p in the last two declarations). The integrals and residues of the chapter, including formula (3) on four integrands, are checked exactly in checks/sage/ch5.py.
